criteria.criterion: A new test, run with `cargo test`, puts job ids that differ between a records worktree and in-tree records/. It shows that Athena::status, the forecast and land_pr's job lookup each see the worktree's job ids and not the in-tree ones.
criteria.evidence: Three tests were added. In status.rs, status_records_worktree_decides_which_jobs_are_listed and forecast_records_worktree_decides_which_classes_are_headlined; in gh/tests.rs, land_pr_records_worktree_decides_which_job_is_found. They commit TREE_JOB 20261010-153012-k7q2 / class-tree into records/ and write WORKTREE_JOB 20261011-090000-z4d8 / class-wt into paths::records_worktree(state.root()). With the worktree present they assert: status lists only WORKTREE_JOB; the forecasts are only class-wt; land_pr(worktree job) fails with 'has no verification' (found) and land_pr(tree job) fails with 'no job matches'. The recorded `cargo test --locked` (CI run for 1b084f7) passed and includes these tests. My own `cargo test -p athena-core records_worktree` could not compile: the shared target dir holds a stale athena-data build from the base source, and `cargo clean` was denied. That is an environment problem, not a code one, because the working tree is clean and paths.rs defines records_worktree. Athena's fails-without-1 run failed (exit 101) only at compile time.

criteria.criterion: A test run with `cargo test` removes the worktree directory and shows that status, the forecast and land_pr's lookup read the in-tree records/ job ids, as before the change.
criteria.evidence: Each of the three tests then calls remove_worktree and asserts the reverse: status lists only TREE_JOB, the forecasts are class-tree, land_pr finds TREE_JOB ('has no verification') and not WORKTREE_JOB ('no job matches'). These pass in the recorded `cargo test --locked`. I ran `cargo test -p athena-gate records` and it passed, including an_absent_worktree_reads_the_in_tree_records (load_current equals load at HEAD), an_existing_worktree_is_read_instead_of_the_in_tree_records, an_empty_existing_worktree_does_not_fall_back and load_dir_sorts_by_path_and_flags_unknown_files. store.rs gained matching unit tests for Records::load_current (covered by the recorded suite).

findings.summary: RecordSet::load_dir ignores read_dir errors at every level, not only an absent records/ root.
findings.evidence: `let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(at) else { return Ok(()); }` is applied to every subdirectory as well. A permission error deep in the worktree would silently drop records instead of reporting them. That contradicts the stated aim that a broken worktree shows as missing or invalid rather than being hidden. A better rule: return Ok only when the root records/ is NotFound, and propagate other errors.

findings.summary: Section 14.2's search scope names crates/athena-cli/src separately, though crates/*/src already covers it.
Athena::status loads the worktree twice (Records and RecordSet) instead of building Records from one RecordSet.
findings.evidence: load_current is called twice with the same worktree. If the directory appeared or changed between the two calls, the two views could differ. Reading one RecordSet::load_current and passing it to Records::from_parts with the landings would remove both the gap and the double read.

summary: The candidate does what the request asks. `records_worktree(state_dir)` is defined once in paths.rs, right after repo_state_dir. `Records::load_current` and `RecordSet::load_current` read the worktree when its directory exists, even when it is empty, and otherwise fall back to records/ at the treeish. Only three readers moved: `Athena::status` (its per-class forecast uses the same records) and `Athena::land_pr`'s job lookup. Every other caller is unchanged. Section 14 of docs/design/records-history.md lists the remaining readers by file and function, and my greps agree with it. CHANGELOG.md has an entry, and no scan test was added. All changed files are on the deliverables list. Tests I ran myself: the gate loader tests (`cargo test -p athena-gate records`, 4 new tests passed) and the path unit test (`cargo test -p athena-data records_worktree`, passed). I could not run the athena-core tests here. The shared build cache (CARGO_TARGET_DIR target/verify) holds an athena-data library built from the base source, apparently left by Athena's "fails without" run. So `cargo test -p athena-core records_worktree` fails to compile with "cannot find function `records_worktree`", even though the clean working tree contains that function (confirmed with git status and Grep). Clearing the cache with `cargo clean` was denied, so I stopped there. For criteria 1 and 2 I rely on the recorded `cargo test --locked` CI pass for commit 1b084f7, which includes those tests, plus my reading of them. Athena's maintainer should clear that stale cache.
